desc:
A matching is a set of edges of the tree such that no two chosen edges share a node. Return the maximum possible number of edges in a matching.

Only the shape of the tree matters, so every node in the input has value 0.

How trees are given. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level order (top to bottom, left to right). The first entry is the root. After that, the left and right child of every existing node are written in turn; a missing child is written as -1 (real node values are never negative). Missing nodes have no children listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped.

For example, [1,2,3,-1,4] is the tree whose root 1 has children 2 and 3; node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child; node 3 is a leaf.

Example 1

tree = [0,0,-1,0,-1,0]
Output: 2
The tree is a path of 4 nodes a-b-c-d. Take edges a-b and c-d.

Example 2

tree = [0,0,0,0,0,0,0]
Output: 2
A perfect tree with 7 nodes: match one leaf with its parent on each side and leave the root free. Every edge uses an inner node, and only the three inner nodes exist, but pairing the root with a child would use two inner nodes in one edge, so 3 edges are impossible.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly
hints: Look at a single node u. Either u is matched to one of its children, or it is not matched inside its own subtree.
Keep two numbers per node: f[u], the best matching inside the subtree of u, and g[u], the best one in which u itself stays unmatched. Then g[u] is the sum of f over the children.
To match u with child c, take g[u] - f[c] + g[c] + 1 (child c must be unmatched below, plus one for the new edge). f[u] is the maximum of g[u] and these options.
editorial: Let f[u] be the largest matching in the subtree of u and g[u] the largest one in which u is not used. Then g[u] = sum of f[c] over the children. If u is matched with child c, then c may not be matched to its own children, so that option is worth g[u] - f[c] + g[c] + 1. Take f[u] as the best of g[u] and all such options; the answer is f[root].

A backwards sweep over the level-order array evaluates it in O(n) time and O(n) memory. A greedy variant also works: process nodes bottom-up and match a node with a child whenever both are still free (leaves first), but the two-state DP is easier to justify, and it is the template for the vertex cover, independent set and dominating set DPs on trees.
solution:
def parse(tree):
    val, left, right = [tree[0]], [-1], [-1]
    i, u = 1, 0
    while u < len(val) and i < len(tree):
        for kids in (left, right):
            if i < len(tree):
                x = tree[i]
                i += 1
                if x != -1:
                    kids[u] = len(val)
                    val.append(x)
                    left.append(-1)
                    right.append(-1)
        u += 1
    return val, left, right


def maxTreeMatching(tree):
    val, left, right = parse(tree)
    n = len(val)
    f = [0] * n
    g = [0] * n
    for u in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        kids = [c for c in (left[u], right[u]) if c != -1]
        base = sum(f[c] for c in kids)
        g[u] = base
        best = base
        for c in kids:
            best = max(best, base - f[c] + g[c] + 1)
        f[u] = best
    return f[0]
